intro: Two per chapter. Pick a side and back it with evidence or economic reasoning from the chapter. Many of these are real debates where thoughtful people disagree.

ratingKey.Green: evidence can settle it, so there's a best answer.
ratingKey.Yellow: evidence matters, but values decide it.
ratingKey.Red: mostly values or opinion, so argue respectfully.

debates.question: Is anything ever truly free?
debates.sideB: No, everything has an opportunity cost

debates.question: Should schools pay students for good grades as an incentive?
debates.sideB: No, learning should be its own reward

debates.question: Is a college degree the best way to build human capital?
debates.sideA: Yes, a degree pays off most
debates.sideB: No, trades and apprenticeships can be just as good

debates.question: Will robots and AI create more jobs than they destroy?
Do market economies do a better job than command economies of producing what people want?
Should the government provide more services, even if taxes go up?
Will people keep buying gas at the same rate if prices double?
debates.sideB: No, people will cut back a lot

debates.question: Does advertising mostly inform buyers or manipulate them?
Should the government subsidize Idaho farmers?
Does a big tax on a product always reduce how much is sold?
debates.sideB: Not always; it depends on elasticity

debates.question: Is it fair for concert tickets to go to whoever pays the most?
debates.sideB: No, use a lottery or limit resale

debates.question: Does rent control help renters overall?
Should the government break up very large tech companies?
Do patents do more good than harm?
debates.sideB: More harm, they keep prices high

debates.question: Is starting your own business worth the risk?
debates.sideA: Yes, the rewards are worth it
debates.sideB: No, a steady job is smarter

debates.question: Should corporate profits be taxed twice (company and dividends)?
Should the federal minimum wage be raised?
Do labor unions help workers more than they hurt businesses?
Would the U.S. be better off going back to the gold standard?
debates.sideB: No, it would limit the economy

debates.question: Should cash be phased out in favor of digital payments?
debates.sideB: No, cash protects privacy and access

debates.question: Are payment apps like Venmo safer than cash?
Should teens open a bank account before they turn 18?
Is investing in the stock market basically gambling?
Should a teen invest in cryptocurrency?
debates.sideA: Yes, it could pay off big

debates.question: Is the 50/30/20 rule realistic for most young adults?
Should college be free at public universities?
debates.sideA: Yes, it's an investment in everyone
debates.sideB: No, students should share the cost

debates.question: Should 18-year-olds be allowed to get credit cards on their own?
debates.sideB: No, require income or a co-signer

debates.question: Is it ever smart to pay only the minimum on a credit card?
debates.sideB: No, the interest is too costly

debates.question: Should health insurance be required for everyone?
debates.sideB: No, it should be a personal choice

debates.question: Is a high insurance deductible a smart choice for young drivers?
Is GDP a good measure of how well people are doing?
Should Idaho try to grow as fast as possible?
debates.sideB: No, growth brings traffic and high housing costs

debates.question: Is inflation worse than unemployment?
Does the official unemployment rate tell the whole story?
debates.sideB: No, it misses discouraged and underemployed workers

debates.question: Can recessions be prevented?
debates.sideB: No, they're part of the cycle

debates.question: Should the government rescue big banks in a crisis?
Is a flat income tax fairer than a progressive one?
Should Idaho remove the sales tax on groceries?
debates.sideB: No, keep the credit and the revenue

debates.question: Is the national debt a serious threat to your future?
Should the federal government be required to balance its budget like Idaho?
debates.sideB: No, it needs room for emergencies

debates.question: Should the Federal Reserve be independent from the President?
debates.sideB: No, it should answer to elected leaders

debates.question: Do higher interest rates help or hurt young people more?
Does trade make both countries better off?
Should the U.S. make more of its own products even if they cost more?
Do tariffs protect American workers?
debates.sideB: No, they raise prices and invite retaliation

debates.question: Is a U.S. trade deficit a problem?
Has globalization been good for the world overall?
debates.sideB: No, it cost too many jobs

debates.question: Should Idaho focus on exporting more or on buying local?
